title: Inmate sentenced for attempted assault of correctional officers in Dutchess Co. - NewsBreak
text:
By Natalie St. Denis ,
1 hours ago
BEEKMAN, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — A man has been sentenced for attempting to assault correctional officers at Green Haven Correctional Facility in Beekman. 43-year-old Edward Gibson was sentenced to 12 years in state prison followed by five years of post-release supervision in Dutchess County Court on Tuesday.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! His sentencing comes after Gibson previously pleaded guilty to first-degree attempted assault in April. The incident originally occurred on July 21, 2025, according to the Dutchess County Attorney’s Office.
Gibson allegedly ran toward a correctional officer, while he was armed with a metal shank, and swung the weapon at her upper body. The officer avoided being struck, but fell to the ground during the incident and injured her knee.
The inmate also allegedly refused multiple lawful commands to surrender and then approached another correctional officer. Gibson admitted to Dutchess County Court that he attempted to cause serious physical injury to the officer by striking him in the back with the metal shank.
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! “The brave men and women who work inside our correctional facilities deserve to know that when they are violently attacked for simply doing their jobs, those responsible will be prosecuted and held accountable,” said Dutchess County District Attorney Anthony Parisi. “This sentence reflects the seriousness of this deliberate and violent attack on correction officers who were working to maintain the safety and security of Green Haven Correctional Facility. Through my Office’s Jail and Prison Violence Prevention Initiative, we have made the prosecution of violence committed within our correctional facilities a priority, working closely with our law enforcement and correctional partners to ensure those who commit these crimes face meaningful consequences that protect correction staff, inmates, and the public alike.”
